translations.source_sense_description: das Ergebnis des Bohrens, das Bohrloch

glosses: To inspire boredom in somebody.

examples.text: to bore someone to death
Reading books really bores me; films are much more exciting.
He bores me with some trick.
[…] used to come and bore me at rare intervals.

glosses: To make a hole through something.

examples.text: I'll believe as soon this whole earth may be bored.
On June 8, 1872, the London & North Western Railway obtained powers to quadruple its main line, and a new tunnel was bored for the up and down slow lines.

glosses: To make a hole with, or as if with, a boring instrument; to cut a circular hole by the rotary motion of a tool.

examples.text: to bore for water or oil
An insect bores into a tree.

glosses: To form or enlarge (something) by means of a boring instrument or apparatus.

examples.text: to bore a steam cylinder or a gun barrel; to bore a hole
short but very powerful jaws, by means whereof the insect can bore […] a cylindrical passage through the most solid wood

glosses: To make (a passage) by laborious effort, as in boring; to force a narrow and difficult passage through.

examples.text: to bore one’s way through a crowd
What bustling crowds I bored.

glosses: To be pierced or penetrated by an instrument that cuts as it turns.

examples.text: This timber does not bore well.

glosses: To glare (as if to drill a hole with the eyes).

examples.text: Their eyes bore into my back.

glosses: To push or drive (a boxer into the ropes, a boat out of its course, etc.).

examples.text: The right hand of Curtis was open too much ; but he nevertheless had the best of the hitting in this round, till Inglis bored him down, out of the ropes.
Hanlan, it seems, led at about a mile, when Beach's steamer bored him, and to avoid the danger of being swamped, he put on a violent spurt and drew well clear of Beach, getting some lengths lead.

glosses: To push forward in a certain direction with laborious effort.

examples.text: They take their flight […] boring to the west.

glosses: To fool; to trick.
